title: The Stairwell and the Count
passages:
Adeyemi dragged Voss across the grating, her boots drumming against the metal. "Don't you dare go dark on me," she said, hauling Voss's limp arm over her shoulder. The amber seam behind them had already closed on empty air, sealing the door bus shut. Senn's mist pooled on the deck plates, thin as wet paper, reaching toward the node chair base where the copper hummed. "I'm still here," Senn said from the vent, voice frayed. "I can short the purge if you get me back inside."

The slate hissed, ink bleeding: *Operator 23 pending. Senn.* Renner's voice, mild and awful out of the wet ink, said, "You gave each half and called it a win." Voss's eyes snapped open behind Adeyemi's grip, clear and not static at all. She stared at the count climbing backward on the slate: 007, 008, 009. "Unfile me," Voss said, voice cracked. "Before it hits zero."

Adeyemi reached the stairwell hatch and shoved it open. A maintenance figure stood silhouetted in the doorway, console glowing amber. "Welcome back," the synthetic voice boomed. "Count is reversing. You've bought minutes. One more step and the purge flips." The figure's smile was a glitch. "Operator 19. Operator 23. Choose."

Adeyemi set Voss down against the rail and reached for the override. "Not a choice," she said. "We take both." She jammed her access key into the console, but the hatch wouldn't budge until the slate stopped writing.

The console flashed red and spat her key back out, slick with something that wasn't oil. *Not yet,* the slate wrote, unbothered. *The hand that files must unfile.* "Wonderful," Adeyemi said. "The furniture has opinions now."

Voss laughed against the rail, a wet and awful sound. "It's not the furniture. It's Renner. He filed me. Only the filing hand reverses it." She rolled her head toward the mist crawling the deck. "And the filing hand is currently a puddle with a grudge."

Senn's voice came thin from the vent. "I can reach the cradle. Tip the busbar and I ride the copper up." A crackle of static. "It'll hurt. I don't have a body to hurt with, but I'm fairly sure it'll hurt."

"Do it," Adeyemi said, and kicked the busbar lever.

The mist gathered itself, no longer paper-thin, and poured toward the node chair base where the copper hummed. The count stuttered—009, 008—then held. Inside the chair something caught. The amber seam along the door bus glowed white and split with a sound like a struck bell. Senn was in. The chair took the shape of a person made of fog and current, and the purge froze at 008, trembling.

"Renner." Voss wasn't looking at the slate anymore. She was looking at the thing in the chair. "You filed Operator 23. Undo it. You always wanted it done *properly*, so do it properly."

The ink bled, gathered, and for one moment the slate showed a hand—Renner's, or the memory of one—reaching back down the page toward her name.

Then it wrote: *Operator 23. Filing reversed at the third mark. Awaiting the fourth.* The maintenance figure's glitching smile widened. "The count resumes when the hand withdraws. It has not withdrawn." And the ink kept moving.
